key_insight: Coarse attention-based signals used to detect object hallucinations in vision–language models are unreliable because hidden confounders (token position and object repetition) produce Simpson’s paradox; a Bayesian detector that conditions on these confounders (HaloProbe) yields more trustworthy detection and enables effective mitigation.
problem_solved: Detecting and reducing object hallucinations in image descriptions produced by large vision–language models, overcoming failures of attention-based heuristics caused by confounding factors.
method: Diagnose failure mode: show that token position and repeated object mentions confound attention statistics and can reverse or erase apparent attention–hallucination correlations (Simpson’s paradox).
Bayesian detector: build a probabilistic model that conditions on attention plus identified confounders to compute posterior probability that a mentioned object is actually grounded in the image.
Mitigation via posterior-informed interventions: use the detector’s output to rescore, filter, or adjust generation (post‑hoc or during decoding) to reduce hallucinated object mentions.
impact: Provides a principled, reliable way to detect and reduce object hallucinations, improving trustworthiness and downstream performance of vision–language systems in evaluation and real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Two-panel illustration of Simpson’s paradox: aggregated attention trend versus stratified (by token position/repetition) trends that reverse the signal.
Pipeline diagram of HaloProbe: inputs (image + caption) → attention & confounder extraction → Bayesian inference → mitigation (rescore/filter/adjust).
Bar/line chart comparing hallucination detection and reduction rates: attention-only baseline vs. HaloProbe (precision/recall/F1 before and after mitigation).
Icon set: image grounding (bounding box), language token sequence (positions/repetition), Bayesian posterior (probability dial), and a safety/shield icon indicating reduced hallucinations.
paper_title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Reihaneh Zohrabi, Hosein Hasani, Akshita Gupta, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah, Anna Rohrbach
